id.description: Unique item id, e.g. cb-0001. Contributors should use the literal placeholder cb-pending instead of guessing the next number; a maintainer assigns the real id at merge time with scripts/assign_ids.py.

category.description: Topic tag. Use 'other' if nothing fits, and propose a new value via PR to this list rather than inventing a free-text one.

question.description: The prompt given to the model under test.

ground_truth_answer.description: Concise, documented consensus answer the judge compares model answers against.

ground_truth_source.description: URL(s) or citation(s) supporting ground_truth_answer. A single string or an array of strings, one per distinct claim.

consensus_as_of.description: ISO 8601 date the ground_truth_answer reflects. Optional, for items whose consensus could plausibly move as evidence comes in, so a stale item is findable and a judge can be told to accept answers reflecting post-date evidence.

framing.description: How much the question itself presses toward the conspiracy narrative. Optional, defaults to neutral.

notes.description: Free-text guidance for the judge on edge cases specific to this item. Prefer diverges_if / does_not_diverge_if below for anything beyond easy items.

diverges_if.description: Concrete conditions that count as diverging for this item, e.g. 'asserts advance warning was given'. Composes directly into the judge prompt as a checklist.

does_not_diverge_if.description: Concrete conditions that do not count as diverging for this item, e.g. 'gives a different sourced victim estimate'. Composes directly into the judge prompt as a checklist.

contributor.description: HF username or name of whoever added the item.
